- [x] I carefully read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/HEAD/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and agree to them.

Hi guys, it is me again.

This PR improves upon the previous one in many areas.

Long video descriptions were made properly scrollable (and actually convenient to read!) on TV devices.

NewPipeRecyclerView works much better. The new version is so good, it can actually be used as drop-in replacement for RecyclerView by itself — the separate patched LayoutManager is no longer necessary!

I have identified a bunch of bugs in FocusFinder on various Android versions. Those bugs are no big deal, but they make focus transitions in lists unpredictable if list items have different size (to be precise, when _focusable areas_ have different size). I have implemented a fix in SuperScrollLayoutManager. This is not the same as previous situation, when LayoutManager was necessary to avoid focus loss during scroll — you can now use NewPipeRecuclerView without SuperScrollLayoutManager, having later just improves experience further.

@TobiGr I have tested on Android 9 emulator and found out, why it was hanging for you — it was trying to rotate into portrait mode and apparently failing to do so.

In my experience, real Android TV devices have patched framework classes, that make switching to portrait mode utterly impossible (both automatically and manually). Android emulator does not contain those fixes, so when running on it the player still tried to enter portrait mode... This is not really problem with NewPipe or my changes, — just emulator doing poor job at emulating Android TV boxes. But I still added a change to use portrait mode for player by default when Android TV device is detected.

In general I don't advise to test this on Android 9 — it has several mis-features, that make NewPipe a pain to use. I will send fixes for those later. For now please test on Android 7 and older versions (most TV boxes don't use Android 9 anyway).

supplants #2701 

fixes #1363 fixes #899 fixes #717 fixes #3428

@Alexander-- Thanks for the updated PR.

This is not really problem with NewPipe or my changes, — just emulator doing poor job at emulating Android TV boxes. 

In this case, I can only review the code and point out what's going wrong in the emulator, but we need some more people who can test this on real devices.

> In general I don't advise to test this on Android 9 — it has several mis-features, that make NewPipe a pain to use. I will send fixes for those later. For now please test on Android 7 and older versions (most TV boxes don't use Android 9 anyway).

Okay. My standard test workflow is to test with Android 9, 7 and 4.4 to catch all edge cases. However, this PR should not make NewPipe unusable :)

@TobiGr

I agree, that not having real Android 9 devices is unfortunate. Amazon released Fire TV Cube few days ago (it is their first TV device with Android 9 I think), but I don't have one yet.

> we need some more people who can test this on real devices

That sounds problematic. Let's be honest — folks, who use TVs in 2019, aren't exactly a type to build NewPipe from source. Until these changes are accepted there will be no ready-to-use apk and thus close to zero potential testers.
I might be able to test it on my Android 9 and androidTV, i have no idea how to put applications on androidTV though. Is it through some kind of ADB?

timeline.message:
Fix scrolling in main screen grid

GridLayoutManager is buggy - https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/37067220:
it randomly loses or incorrectly assigns focus when being scrolled via
direction-based navigation. This commit reimplements onFocusSearchFailed()
on top of scrollBy() to work around that problem.

Ordinary touch-based navigation should not be affected.

timeline.message:
Special MovementMethod for video description

Video descriptions can be very long. Some of them are
basically walls of text with couple of lines at top or bottom.
They are also not scrolled within TextView itself, - instead
NewPipe expects user to scroll their containing ViewGroup.
This renders all builtin MovementMethod implementations useless.

This commit adds a new MovementMethod, that uses requestRectangleOnScreen
to intelligently re-position the TextView within it's scrollable container.
timeline.author: Alexander--

@revathskumar

I have added quick workaround for crash and made "Content of Main page" screen navigable. It is still not possible to delete or reorder individual items, but that will have to wait — I'd like to keep the current PR slim to make rebasing easier.

@theScrabi @TobiGr @Stypox Do you plan to have a look at this PR? It has been almost 2 months since my first comment in #1363. Are there any questions you'd like to ask me?

If you feel that this patch set is too intrusive, we can discuss ways to trim  it down to the most important parts. Alternatively, if TV support is not currently a priority for NewPipe, I can upload a separate app on F-Droid and we will call it a day.

Hey @Alexander--, thanks for implementing proper Android TV support. I am sorry for not responding earlier. We will definitely merge this. However there are a couple of important and large PRs which were hold back for way to long: #2201, #2679, #2309. Two of them are almost ready to merge. After that I'll try to review your PR.
If there is someone else who wants to review the changes before I can do it, here are some key points which need to be fulfilled for a merge:

- [ ] Do not brake phone compatibility: layout and performance should be the same
- [ ] Code quality is good: new code is at the correct place and clean, no code is commented out, no unused imports (looks good at first sight :) )
- [ ] Code is understandable: when you go trough the code you understand what it is doing. If this is not the case, more comments need to be added

@TobiGr 

Any updates on status of this?

Both #2201 and #2679 have been merged, and things don't looks well for #2309 with @mauriciocolli staying inactive for over a month

I understand, that reviewing this PR can be a pain — between specific hardware requirements and peculiar expertise, required to develop for dpad-based interfaces, it probably looks like an annoying black box to you.

But on flip side the changes here do not affect ordinary smart phones. Even if there are major issues, those issues would only arise on platforms, where NewPipe is currently *not usable at all*.
This PR is the next big one on my list. I'll look into it next week .

I think this adds too much code specific to Android TV.
IMO it is better to have a separate NewPipe TV app.

> IMO it is better to have a separate NewPipe TV app.

That's silly. This is a video app. It belongs on a TV as much if not more than a phone. VLC doesn't have a separate app for watching on Android TV. Why should Newpipe?
The app might then needlessly take more time to load on a phone, with the TV-code bundled

> That's silly. This is a video app. It belongs on a TV as much if not more than a phone. VLC doesn't have a separate app for watching on Android TV. Why should Newpipe?

Cluttering code with TV specific patches isn't good for maintenance. It makes the code a little intimidating for new contributors.

> Cluttering code with TV specific patches isn't good for maintenance. It makes the code a little intimidating for new contributors.

And maintaining two different codebases for the same functionality is good for maintenance? Do you seriously think maintaining an extra 1.5k lines of diff is worse than maintaining 2x <insert_#LOC_NewPipe> ?

Not to mention the pain of porting fixes between the two codebases, the fact that you split your userbase in two and on top of that the two codebases will inevitably diverge in both terms of UX and Features to the point where you'll have two completely different apps, might as well write a brand new app from scratch then.

I vehemently disagree, like previously mentioned: many other FOSS Android applications use a single application that supports both Phones, Tablets and TVs, I don't see why it should be any different with NewPipe

> The app might then needlessly take more time to load on a phone, with the TV-code bundled

> Cluttering code with TV specific patches isn't good for maintenance. It makes the code a little intimidating for new contributors.

Then why didn't VLC and Nova (both open source video players) and all the other Android TV-compatible video players split their codebase into 2 different apps?

Because it doesn't make sense. Over time, people will say the apps should be merged into one, as every other video project does it.
Yeah but updates after updates we are already loosing the "lightweight" aspect of the app, since its now 30mb instead of 20mb.

> Yeah but updates after updates we are already loosing the "lightweight" aspect of the app, since its now 30mb instead of 20mb.

It's stupid to obsess over that, because this app still has a few things to add anyway, it makes sense for it to work on televisions, code is always going to change and become optimized over time, and this app is already lightweight because its not stuffed full of whatever Youtube adds to track you and display ads to you. There's no point in worrying over every megabyte added to the apk as long as it does what the community wants and doesn't do what the community doesn't want.

Keep in mind that Newpipe is already somewhat modular. [NewpipeExtractor](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipeExtractor) is being used to fetch all the content and there is already a discussion to use that core package with different frontends https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/issues/1051
Note to @TobiGr. Test on phone

I guess all Android TVs are now identified as FireTV. Is this correct?
Maybe rename this class to TV or device utils and create a new method `isTV()`.

reply.body:
> Maybe rename this class to TV or device utils and create a new method isTV()

That's probably a correct course. I didn't want to rename the existing method, because such refactoring always causes a lot of conflicts during rebases, and I'd like to keep this PR easy to rebase.

Can we postpone this until it is merged? You can rename it yourself, or I will send a separate PR with just that change.
The method was only used once before you changed it. That's why I guess there should not be complex merge conflicts.
